section.linux-notes.title: Linux compatibility and support
section.linux-notes.sub: Watchdog, Workshop, mods, ports and community VPS notes.
section.linux-notes.b0.0: Source: official Co-op Discord setup, FAQ and Linux-support notes, reviewed 6 November 2026. Community recipes remain unverified unless stated otherwise.
section.linux-notes.b1.d0.b0.0: Official Co-op Discord setup notes (6 November 2026): Workshop item 3770450698 contains DedicatedServer/BannerlordCoopServer.exe under steamapps/workshop/content/261550/3770450698/. For a manual install, extract the matching latest client so Modules/Coop/SubModule.xml exists. Enable only Co-op for the baseline test, disable other mods and War Sails, and choose No to Safe Mode. Do not combine a manual Modules/Coop copy with the Workshop module; back up and remove the redundant manual copy when switching. Workshop updates require TaleWorlds approval and may lag the release; check versions rather than assuming parity.
section.linux-notes.b1.summary.0: Install from Workshop or manually — not both
section.linux-notes.b2.d0.b0.0: Launch the Linux client through Steam. For SteamAPI_Init failed, restart Steam when safe; first confirm no running server depends on it. Do not change an active game or server session during a test.
section.linux-notes.b3.d0.b0.0: Official Discord reports describe renaming the client bin/Win64_Shipping_Client/watchdog directory to a backup name to reduce world-map stutter on Bazzite, CachyOS and Arch. Developer caveat: disabling it removes crash logs needed for support. Only do this with explicit permission, while the game is closed, and retain the backup so it can be restored. --no-watchdog is a SERVER argument only, not a client launch option. Issue: https://github.com/Bannerlord-Coop-Team/BannerlordCoop/issues/2536.
section.linux-notes.b4.d0.b0.0: Add BannerlordCoopServer.exe as a non-Steam game, select GE-Proton and put --no-watchdog in the server launch options. Alternatively use the game’s Proton prefix. For safety testing, use a separate prefix and --data-dir, not an existing live server prefix or save directory. A Steam-listed lobby under Proton/Wine is still unverified; direct IP is the reproducible fallback.
section.linux-notes.b5.d0.b0.0: Official Discord direct-IP instructions use steam:false in server-config.json and UDP 4200–4201 through the host firewall, router and cloud firewall. The configured main port defaults to 4200. Steam player-hosting Join Game/invites can avoid port forwarding and CGNAT; do not assume dedicated-server Steam hosting under Proton/Wine has the same verified behavior. Turn off conflicting VPN/DNS-routing tools only after considering other active sessions.
section.linux-notes.b6.d0.b0.0: Gameplay and difficulty settings live in CoopData/mod-config.json; server settings in CoopData/DedicatedServer/server-config.json. Workshop layouts can also use DedicatedServer/server-data/mod-config.json. Confirm active paths at boot and stop only the intended server before editing. Keys include battleSize (default 1000; about 400 suggested), autoPauseEnabled, goldFoodInfluenceChangeInSettlements, enablePlayerExecutions and enableHeroExecutions. Difficulty birth/death options include birthAndDeath, clanMemberDeathChance and battleDeath; keep the separate Birth and Aging module disabled.
section.linux-notes.b7.d0.b0.0: First verify Coop-only operation. Copy a compatible mod folder into engine/Modules; its folder name must match the mod Id. In the server UI reload, enable, set load order and Save Mods, then restart only that intended server. Every client needs matching mods, versions and order. Official Discord reports War Sails, Birth and Aging Options and Fast Mode are unsupported on dedicated servers. Do not alter Steam subscriptions automatically.
section.linux-notes.b8.d0.b0.0: Dedicated logs: CoopData/DedicatedServer/logs/coop-server-{date}-{time}.log. Client: bin/Win64_Shipping_Client/Coop_client.log; in-game host: Coop_server.log. Case matters on Linux. Crashes can be under the prefix’s drive_c/ProgramData/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/crashes or Documents/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/Coop Crash Reports. Keep the crash report (the Send action can remove it), redact secrets and use the official support-ticket channel. Do not repeatedly rejoin a stalled session.
section.linux-notes.b9.d0.b0.0: Headless dedicated-server SERVING was validated in this guide’s disposable tests with WineHQ Wine 11.0 (image docker.io/tianon/wine:11.0.0 / winehq-stable 11.0.0 on Debian trixie) plus Xvfb. Debian stock Wine 8.0 failed the same recipe (virtual_setup_exception stack overflow; no SERVING). Wine 9 and 10 were not tested here — treat 11.0 as the validated version, not a proven minimum across every Wine release. Do not use distro apt/yum “wine” metapackages that resolve to Wine 8 as an end-to-end recommendation. Preserve the Workshop layout (DedicatedServer alongside bin/, GUI/, SubModule.xml). Prefer host networking for UDP; keep stdin_open/tty for the console. GPU is not required for SERVING; a display server (Xvfb is enough; some setups need MIT-SHM disabled) is. Official Discord also mentions Ubuntu + Wine + winbind + Xvfb as community hosting notes.
section.linux-notes.b9.summary.0: VPS / Docker / Wine — validated Wine 11.0 headless path
section.linux-notes.b10.d0.b0.0: The bannerlordcoop-server-manager project and the Unofficial Bannerlord Co-op Pterodactyl egg are community tools, not official support. Review their source and compatibility before use. This guide does not install them.
section.linux-notes.b11.d0.b0.0: The official FAQ says Linux is supported but Steam Deck is not; Deck reports vary (https://github.com/Bannerlord-Coop-Team/BannerlordCoop/issues/2162). Hosting and playing together is estimated at 8 CPU cores and 16 GB RAM, with a dedicated server. A running game instance is not required for dedicated hosting. Linux host-and-play transfer stalls are tracked in issue #2095.
section.linux-notes.b12.d0.b0.0: Compare full Bannerlord build identifiers as well as Co-op releases. Even minor build differences can stall joining. Check the server log for the refused build or mod. Save cleanly, stop only the intended server, then back up CoopData and any distribution server-data before replacing files. Never automate Workshop unsubscribe/resubscribe or restart Steam during someone’s active session.
section.linux-notes.b12.summary.0: Exact game builds and safe updates
section.linux-notes.b13.d0.b0.0: Windows exit -1073741819 indicates access violation; check blocked/missing DLLs and retained save backups. -532462766 indicates an unhandled .NET exception. Exit 1 is generic. Exit 25 points to ProgramData/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/logs/starter_log.txt inside the prefix. Diagnose from the preceding log messages, not the number alone. These official FAQ diagnostics were not deliberately reproduced here.
section.linux-notes.b14.d0.b0.0: This guide uses distributed Win64 binaries. Native .NET server work is tracked at https://github.com/Bannerlord-Coop-Team/BannerlordCoop/issues/2843; repository visibility is not permission to self-build or redistribute. The TAOM client launcher is Windows-only and is reported not to work under Proton/Wine. Other mods are not guaranteed; establish a Co-op-only baseline first.

distro.bazzite.blurb: A gaming-ready immutable OS built on Fedora that updates as a single image (Silverblue-style systems fit here too).
distro.deck.blurb: Valve's handheld and its SteamOS: a read-only system, so use Desktop Mode and keep changes small.
distro.nix.blurb: A declarative, reproducible Linux that is configured entirely through Nix.
distro.other.name: Other distro
distro.other.blurb: Gentoo, Void, Alpine or anything else: you get the generic commands to adapt.
ui.oneScriptSub: One copy-paste script for your distro.
